targets.title: Facial redness, expression, and masculinity influence perceptions of anger and health.

targets.outcome_quote:
Although our results do not cast any doubt on the robustness of the red-anger effect in

within-subjects designs, we did not observe the red-anger effect at first impression, which

suggests that demand characteristics have been driving the effect. Thus, we consider previous

findings to be a method-dependent phenomenon.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The main message is that the observed effect depends on demand characteristics: replicated within-subjects results are argued to reflect an invalid inference about spontaneous emotion perception. The special flawed verdict takes precedence over ordinary mixed close/conceptual results.

reasoning: Verified title and all four authors on OSF primary PDF. Both studies retest Young et al. Study 1. Other facial-redness studies motivate the work rather than being separately specified targets.
